# Equipment Lending Rules
Fenwray Film Society is a fictional organisation.

Adopted: 26 February 2025
Effective: 1 March 2025

## 1. Eligibility and reservations
1.1 Only active members aged 18 or over may borrow equipment.
1.2 Bookings must be requested at least three calendar days ahead.
1.3 Requests are recorded in order of receipt.
1.4 A booking is confirmed when the hire fee and deposit are received.
1.5 Equipment cannot be booked for dates reserved for society screenings.

## 2. Hire period
2.1 A booking day runs from 12:00 noon until 12:00 noon the next day.
2.2 Equipment may be hired for no more than three consecutive booking days.
2.3 An extension requires approval before the original return deadline.
2.4 Extensions are charged using the rates in film-fees.md.

## 3. Deposits and collection
3.1 The refundable security deposit is £80 per booking.
3.2 One deposit covers the projector and screen when hired together.
3.3 The borrower must present their membership number at collection.
3.4 The equipment officer records its condition before handover.
3.5 The borrower signs the collection and condition record.

## 4. Use and responsibility
4.1 Equipment may be used indoors only.
4.2 Borrowers must not lend it to another person.
4.3 The projector and screen must remain in their protective cases during transport.
4.4 Borrowers must report faults within 24 hours of discovering them.
4.5 Safety precautions are specified in film-safety.md.

## 5. Returns and charges
5.1 Returns are accepted between 10:00 and 16:00 by arrangement.
5.2 A late return costs £10 for each started 24-hour period.
5.3 The deposit is returned within seven calendar days after inspection.
5.4 Documented damage costs may be deducted from the deposit.
5.5 Any deduction must be itemised and sent to the borrower.
5.6 Hire refunds are governed by film-refunds.md.

# Volunteer Front-Desk Quick Guide
Fenwray Film Society is a fictional organisation.

Prepared: 8 April 2025
Last reviewed: 15 July 2025

This sheet is for quick answers, not formal decisions.
The governing documents prevail over this summary.
Check film-changes.md for later decisions before quoting a figure.

## 1. Joining the society
1.1 People aged 16 and over can apply.
1.2 Under-18s need a parent or guardian's written agreement.
1.3 Adults pay roughly £25 to £30 annually.
1.4 Younger members pay £12 annually.
1.5 Membership usually runs to the end of February.
1.6 Ask the secretary if someone has recently renewed.

## 2. Coming to a film
2.1 Public screenings are normally held twice monthly.
2.2 Standard admission is £7.
2.3 Members usually pay around £4 or £5.
2.4 Children have lower prices depending on age.
2.5 Reservations open about two weeks before the film.
2.6 Seats are limited, so advance payment is recommended.

## 3. Borrowing the equipment
3.1 Adult members may borrow the projector or screen.
3.2 Bookings need a few days' notice.
3.3 The projector costs £18 per day and the screen £8.
3.4 Taking both together costs £23 per day.
3.5 Expect a refundable deposit of around £80 to £100.
3.6 The usual loan is a few days, subject to the current limit.

## 4. Cancellations and problems
4.1 Early ticket cancellation normally qualifies for a refund.
4.2 Equipment cancellation may result in a partial charge.
4.3 The society refunds tickets when it cancels a screening.
4.4 Report faulty equipment promptly to the equipment officer.

## 5. Before giving a definite answer
5.1 Check the relevant governing document and changes register.
5.2 Do not promise an exception without committee authority.

content.text:
**Yes, you're allowed three consecutive booking days.**

- **The rule that applies:** Section 2.2 of the Equipment Lending Rules (`film-equipment.md`) says equipment may be hired for no more than three consecutive booking days. That rule was effective from 1 March 2025. A booking day runs from noon to noon (2.1). Collecting at noon on 6 May 2025 would therefore take you to noon on 9 May.
- **Later changes don't affect you:** The only amendment to the hire limit is the committee decision of 12 March 2026. It raised the maximum to five days from 1 April 2026, and it goes by the scheduled first collection date (4.3). Your collection date of 6 May 2025 is before that, so the original three-day limit governs.
- **The two-day limit:** I found no two-day limit in the equipment rules or the changes register. Whoever told you that was mistaken.
- **Notice period:** Section 1.2 requires bookings to be requested at least three calendar days ahead. You asked on 28 April for a 6 May collection, so you met that.

Your booking is only confirmed once the hire fee and deposit are received (1.4). Also, the equipment can't be booked for dates reserved for society screenings (1.5). I didn't check whether 6–9 May 2025 clashes with a screening.
